segments.heading: File header: input, output and rules
segments.text:
Header comment of the script. It names the output (one HTML page) and the input (`facts.json`), and it lists the rules of the script:
- No measured number is typed. Each one is computed from the interval records.
- For a bwx record, `val` (line 176) sums the thread rows of the raw csv file that the record names.
- A wrong record count stops the build.
- A mismatch with `FACTS.md` or with the verdict records of `facts.json` is printed in the self-check list. The page is then not written, and the exit status is 1.
Modules of the Python standard library. No other package is needed. `Decimal` and `ROUND_HALF_UP` are used for rounding (function `q`, line 90).

Fixed paths. `S` is the scratch folder of the rerun, which holds `facts.json` and `FACTS.md`. `R` is the results folder with the raw csv files. `OUT` is the page that the script writes, and `EARLIER` is the earlier report page.
Colours of the page as hexadecimal codes. The comment assigns `BLUE` to the old read kernel and `ORANGE` to the load-only loop.

Two lists that start empty. `CHECKS` collects the lines of the self-check list, each as a pair (pass or fail, text). `PROSE` collects the prose of the page for the word count. The comment names what is not counted: tables, captions, the word list and the references.

segments.heading: Function `stop`: end the script with a message
segments.text: `sys.exit` with a text prints the text to the error output and ends the script with exit status 1. No later line runs. The page is written only at the end of the file. So a stop leaves the page on disk as it was.

segments.heading: Function `need`: hard assertion
segments.text: When `cond` is false, it calls `stop` with the message. When `cond` is true, nothing happens. The script uses it to assert record counts, the content of raw csv rows, and the expected results of comparisons.

segments.heading: Function `check`: one line of the self-check list
segments.text: Appends the pair (pass or fail, text) to `CHECKS`. The script continues after a failed check. The end of the file prints the list. It writes the page only when every line passed.

segments.heading: Function `grouped`: join many checks into one line
segments.text: Removes from `CHECKS` all checks that were added since position `start`. It adds one check in their place. The new line states how many of the comparisons were equal, and it passes only when all were equal. After a failure the line also holds the text of the first failed comparison.

segments.heading: Function `read_retry`: read a file, up to 10 tries
segments.text: Reads the whole file and returns `parse(text)`. It waits 1.5 s and tries again in three cases: the file cannot be read (`OSError`), the parse fails (`ValueError`), or `complete(text)` is false. After 10 failed tries it calls `stop`. The comment gives the reason: another agent rebuilds the two input files from time to time, and a read can then find a file that is only partly written.

segments.heading: Function `lines_of`: the lines of a text file
segments.text: Returns the lines of a file as a list, without the line ends. A byte that is not valid UTF-8 is replaced by a replacement character. So the read does not fail on such a byte.

segments.heading: Function `D`: convert a number to `Decimal`
segments.text: Returns a `Decimal` unchanged. Any other number is converted through its text form. So the floating-point number 467.83 becomes exactly the decimal value 467.83.

segments.heading: Function `q`: round to a step
segments.text: Rounds `x` to the step `places`, which is 0.01 by default. A value exactly between two steps is rounded away from zero: 462.295 becomes 462.30. The functions `f2`, `f1` and `signed` call it.

segments.heading: Functions `f2` and `f1`: number to text
segments.text: `f2` rounds with `q` to 0.01 and returns the text with 2 decimals. The script prints rates in GB/s with it. `f1` rounds to 0.1 and returns the text with 1 decimal. The script prints percent values with it.

segments.heading: Function `median`: the middle value
segments.text: Sorts the values. For an odd count it returns the middle value. For an even count it returns the mean of the two middle values. The result is not rounded here.

segments.heading: Function `esc`: make a text safe for HTML
segments.text: Replaces the characters `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` by their HTML codes. So a value cannot change the structure of the page.

Two dictionaries that start empty. `_FILES` keeps the lines of every csv file that `file_lines` has read. `_TROWS` keeps the T rows of every csv file that `t_rows` has read, grouped by interval. So `file_lines` reads each csv file from disk only once.

segments.heading: Function `file_lines`: the csv file of a record
segments.text: A record names its csv file with two fields: `folder`, for example `R/w120-T72L1-20261117T221329Z`, and `file`, for example `a6456.csv`. The function removes the first `R/` from `folder` and joins the results folder `R` (line 30), the rest and `file` to one path. It reads the file with `lines_of` and keeps the lines in `_FILES`. Line 1 of the file is element 0 of the list.

segments.heading: Function `t_rows`: the 120 thread rows of a bwx12 record
segments.text:
Returns the T rows of the interval of one bwx12 record. Each T row holds one thread.
- First call for a csv file: every line that starts with `T,` is split at the commas into `p`. The script stops when such a line does not have 13 fields.
- The rows are grouped by round, position and kernel: `p[1]`, `p[2]`, `p[3]`. Python counts from 0. So `p[1]` is field 2.
- Six values are kept per row: `p[5]` cpu, `p[6]` bytes, `p[7]` elapsed_s, `p[9]` t_start_s, `p[10]` t_end_s, and the line number. The names are the column names of the csv header [Ref4]. The fields tid, t_sched_s, passes and flags are not read.
- Then the function takes the rows with the round, position and kernel of the record. The script stops unless they are exactly 120.
- The script also stops unless these rows are the 120 lines directly after the I row of the record (field `line`).
- The key holds no process number. If a file held the same round, position and kernel in two processes, the count would be above 120 and the script would stop.

segments.heading: Function `t_rows_block`: the same for the older runner bwx
segments.text:
Returns the T rows of one record of the older runner bwx, in the form of `t_rows`. A csv file of that runner holds several processes. So the rows are taken by their place in the file.
- It reads the 120 lines directly after the I row of the record (field `line`).
- The script stops unless each of these lines has 13 fields, `T` in the first field, and the round, position and kernel of the record.
- The script also stops when the next line after these 120 starts with `T,`. So exactly 120 T rows follow the I row.

segments.heading: Function `i_row_rate`: the rate printed in the I row
segments.text: Splits the line that the record names (field `line`) at the commas. The script stops unless the line has 9 fields, `I` in the first field, the round, position and kernel of the record, and 120 in the field threads (`p[5]`). The function returns `p[8]`, the field aggregate_GBps, as a `Decimal`. The runner computed this printed rate as the bytes of all threads divided by the longest elapsed time of one thread [Ref4].

segments.heading: Function `file_process`: check the csv row of a part A record
segments.text:
- It splits the line that the record names (field `line`) at the commas into `p`.
- The script stops unless the line has 10 fields, `p[0]` is the kernel of the record, `p[1]` (threads) is 120, `p[3]` (rep) is the interval number of the record, and `p[6]` (aggregate_GBps) equals the field `GBps` of the record [Ref3].
- The row holds no name of a binary, and this function does not compare the binary.
- It returns the number of lines that start with `-- ` from line 1 of the file up to this row. Each such line is the header line of one process. So the result is the number of the process inside the file, counted from 1.

segments.heading: Function `val`: the rate of one record in GB/s
segments.text:
Returns the rate of one interval record in GB/s. The class `Rg` and the function `drops_of` take their rates from here.
- Part A record: it returns the field `GBps` of the record. Nothing is summed. This is the rate that the benchmark printed in the csv row with 2 decimals: the bytes of all threads divided by the longest elapsed time of one thread [Ref3].
- Other records: it takes the 120 T rows from `t_rows` when the binary is bwx12, else from `t_rows_block`.
- Line 186 computes `bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9` for each T row: the rate of one thread in GB/s, with 1 GB = 1e9 bytes. So each thread is divided by its own elapsed time. This formula differs from the formula of part A.
- It adds the rates of the threads with a CPU number below 64 (mesh 0), then the rates of the other threads (mesh 1), then the two sums. All 120 rows are in the sum. `facts_data.py` adds in the same order, and `build_facts.py` (named in the comment of lines 177 to 181) takes its sum from there.
- Line 187: the script stops unless the sum, rounded to 3 decimals, equals the field `GBps` of the record.
- Line 188 stores the sum, rounded to 6 decimals, in the record as `_exact`. Every later call returns the stored value. Example: 462.300017 GB/s for the first interval of part L in session 1, where the I row prints 462.29 GB/s [Ref4].

segments.heading: Class `Rg`: the range of a group of records
segments.text:
An `Rg` object holds the rates of a list of records and their lowest-to-highest range.
- The script stops when the list is empty.
- `recs`: the records, sorted by the launch time of their process (`launch_utc`) and then by the interval number.
- `v`: the rate of each record from `val`, in this order.
- `lo`, `hi`, `med`: the lowest rate, the highest rate and the median of `v`. No record of the list is left out.
- `n`: the number of records, which is the number of intervals.
- `procs` and `np`: the different values of the field `proc_key`, and their count, which is the number of processes.

`txt` returns the text `lowest to highest`, each rate with 2 decimals. `overlaps` is true when the two ranges share at least one value. Two ranges that share exactly one value count as overlapping. The test uses the rates as `val` returns them (6 decimals for a bwx record), not the rounded text.

`nearest` returns 0 when the two ranges overlap. Else it returns the gap between the two nearest ends in GB/s: above 0 when this range is the higher one, below 0 when it is the lower one. `farthest` returns the larger of the two differences `self.hi - other.lo` and `other.hi - self.lo`. For two ranges that do not overlap, this is the highest end of the higher range minus the lowest end of the lower range.

segments.heading: Function `plural`: a count with its word
segments.text: Returns the count and the word, for example `1 process`, `3 processes` or `6 intervals`. For a count other than 1 it adds `es` to a word that ends in `s`, and `s` to any other word.

segments.heading: Function `signed`: a value with its sign
segments.text: Rounds the value to 0.01 with `q`. It returns `0` when the rounded value is zero. Else it returns the sign `+` or `-` and the value with 2 decimals, for example `-1.24`.

segments.heading: Function `facts_complete`: is `FACTS.md` complete
segments.text: True when the text holds the heading `## 7. Files` and the phrase `Output files of this sheet`. In `FACTS.md` section 7 is the last section, and the phrase is in the last line of the file. So a file that is only partly written fails the test, and `read_retry` tries again.

segments.heading: Load `facts.json` and `FACTS.md`
segments.text:
- `FJ` is `facts.json`, parsed with `json.loads`. `FMD` is the text of `FACTS.md`.
- `IV` is the list of all interval records. The record groups below are selected from this list.
- `META` is the part `meta` of `facts.json`, and `RERUN` is `meta.rerun`.
- The script stops when the number of records in `IV` differs from `meta.counts.intervals`. The file states 793 records [Ref2].

segments.heading: Function `sel`: select records by field values
segments.text:
Returns the records of `IV` that pass every test of the call, in the order of `IV`. Each argument names a record field and gives a test for it. Example: `sel(dataset="rerun-L", kernel="oldread", pos=0)` returns the records whose field `dataset` is `rerun-L`, whose `kernel` is `oldread` and whose `pos` is 0.
- A plain value: the field must be equal to it.
- A list, tuple or set: the field value must be one of its elements.
- A function: it must return true for the field value.

segments.heading: Function `expect`: assert the size of a group
segments.text: The script stops unless the list has exactly `n` records, they come from exactly `nproc` processes (different values of `proc_key`), and every record has 120 threads. The function returns the list unchanged. `what` names the group in the stop message.
The names of the 8000 MT/s datasets. `LPOOL` lists the bwx12 rows L-1 to L-4, and `APOOL` lists the part A rows A-1 to A-3.

segments.heading: Record groups: part A at 7200 MT/s
segments.text:
- `A_OLD`: dataset `rerun-A`, binary `bw_old`, kernel `read`. This is the old read kernel.
- `A_NEW`: the same with the binary `bw_new`. This is the new read kernel.
- Each group must have 18 intervals of 6 processes.
- The part A intervals of the kernels write, copy, asmread, asmwrite and asmcopy are not selected.

segments.heading: Record groups: the part L line at 7200 MT/s
segments.text:
- Three datasets hold runs of the argument line of part L in the 7200 MT/s boot: `rerun-L` (part L), `control-I` (control I) and `F72d12`.
- For each, the group that ends in `_OLD` holds `oldread` at position 0, and the group that ends in `_ASM` holds `asmread` at position 1.
- Expected size of each group: part L 6 intervals of 3 processes, control I 4 of 2, F72d12 2 of 1.
- The intervals of read_nop96, read_nop256 and read_1pl of these processes are not selected.

segments.heading: Record groups: part C at 7200 MT/s
segments.text:
- `C_OLD`, `C_READ`, `C_ASM`: all part C intervals of `oldread`, `read` and `asmread`, at any position. Each group must have 8 intervals of 4 processes.
- `C_READ_AO`: the `read` intervals whose field `kernel_before` is `oldread`. These are the 4 intervals of the two cfwd processes.
- `C_READ_AA`: the `read` intervals timed directly after `asmread`. These are the 4 intervals of the two crev processes.
- `C_ASM_AR`, `C_ASM_AO`, `C_ASM_FI`: the `asmread` intervals directly after `read` (4 intervals), directly after `oldread` (2), and first in their process (2). Each of the three groups comes from 2 processes.

segments.heading: Record groups: bwx12 rows at 8000 MT/s
segments.text:
- `B_L_OLD[d]` and `B_L_ASM[d]`: for each dataset `d` of L-1 to L-4, `oldread` at position 0 and `asmread` at position 1.
- Expected size per kernel: L-1 2 intervals of 1 process, L-2 4 of 2, L-3 2 of 1, L-4 3 of 3.
- `P_L_OLD` and `P_L_ASM`: the four datasets joined to one pool per kernel. Each pool must have 11 intervals of 7 processes.

segments.heading: Record groups: part A rows at 8000 MT/s
segments.text:
- `B_A_OLD[d]`: kernel `read` of `bw_old` in A-1, A-2 and A-3. Expected sizes: 6 intervals of 2 processes, 6 of 2, and 9 of 3.
- `B_A_NEW[d]`: kernel `read` of `bw_new` in A-1 and A-2, 6 intervals of 2 processes each. No A-3 group is built for `bw_new`.
- `P_A_OLD`: the pool A-1 to A-3 for `bw_old`, 21 intervals of 7 processes. No pool is built for `bw_new`.

segments.heading: All used records: modules, speed and boot
segments.text:
- `USED` holds every record of the groups above once. The expected sizes add up to 139 records.
- The script stops unless every record of `USED` comes from a run with 12 memory modules.
- `SEVEN` and `EIGHT`: the records at 7200 MT/s and at 8000 MT/s. The script stops when a record has another speed.
- All 7200 MT/s records must have the boot id of the rerun (`meta.rerun.boot_id`). All 8000 MT/s records must share one value of the field `boot`.
- The 7200 MT/s records must come from exactly these datasets: `rerun-A`, `rerun-L`, `rerun-C`, `control-I`, `F72d12`.

The method fields of the used records. The script stops unless all hold:
- Part A records: `min_ms` is 500 (an interval lasts at least 0.5 s) and `stop` is `whole pass`.
- All other records: `stop` is `common`.
- Part L, part C, control I, F72d12 and L-1: `min_ms` is 6000 (6 s).
- L-2, L-3 and L-4: `min_ms` is 4000 (4 s). So the pool L-1 to L-4 holds 6 s intervals and 4 s intervals.

segments.heading: Records of the older runner bwx
segments.text:
- `BWX_POOL`: four datasets of the older runner bwx: B7a, B7b, C3a and C3b. The comment says that the rules file names them as the reference of part C, and that the page shows them in one note under Table 2.
- `X_READ_AO`: `read` at position 1. `X_READ_AA`: `read` at position 6. `X_ASM_AR`: `asmread` at position 2. Each must have 48 intervals of 24 processes.
- `X_LOADS`: all `read` and `asmread` intervals of these datasets, 192 intervals of 24 processes. Besides the three groups it holds 48 `asmread` intervals at position 5 (counted in `facts.json` for this companion).
- The script stops unless the kernel directly before is `oldread`, `asmread` and `read` for the three groups, in this order.
- It also stops unless every tag of `X_LOADS` starts with `common-6000-`.

- `X_REV_READ`, `X_REV_ASM`: `read` and `asmread` of the datasets B5a-rev and B5b-rev. Each must have 4 intervals of 4 processes. The comment says that these processes ran the reverse kernel order.
- `OTHER` joins `X_LOADS` and these two groups. The expected sizes add up to 200 records.
- The script stops unless every record of `OTHER` has the binary `bwx`, 12 modules, 8000 MT/s, the common stop and `min_ms` 6000.
- It also stops unless the records of `OTHER` come from the boot of the other 8000 MT/s records.

Adds the first line of the self-check list, with the fixed result PASS. The script reaches this line only when all hard assertions above have passed. The line states the number of used records and of bwx records.

segments.heading: Sum of the T rows against the rate of the I row
segments.text:
- `BWX_USED`: the records of `USED` outside part A. All of them are bwx12 records.
- For each record, `val` gives the sum of the 120 T rows. This sum is rounded to 0.01 GB/s, and the rate printed in the I row (`i_row_rate`) is subtracted. `IROW_MAX` is the largest absolute difference.
- The script stops when `IROW_MAX` is above 0.02 GB/s. The same test runs for the records of `OTHER` with `IROW_MAX_X`.
- These are the first calls of `val`. So the T rows of all bwx12 records of `USED` and of all records of `OTHER` are read and checked here.
- In these lines the printed rate is only compared. The page value is the sum of the T rows.
- In the saved output of a build both largest differences are 0.02 GB/s [Ref5].

segments.heading: Part A: the csv row and the process number
segments.text:
- `A_USED`: the part A records of `USED`. For each one, `file_process` checks the csv row and returns the number of the process inside the file. The number is stored in the record as `_fproc`.
- The script stops when `_fproc` differs from the field `process` of a record. The A-3 records are left out of this test.
- For A-3 the two numbers differ (checked for this companion): `facts.json` numbers the three A-3 processes 1, 2 and 3, and in the file `A3.csv` they are the processes 1, 3 and 5.
- Lines 351 to 353 add the second line of the self-check list, with the fixed result PASS. It holds the record counts and the two largest differences.

segments.heading: Function `src`: source text for a tooltip
segments.text: Returns the source text of a value for a tooltip: the csv file and the line numbers of the records. The script stops when one call mixes part A records and bwx records. For part A the lines are the interval rows that hold the rates. For bwx records the lines are the I rows, and the text adds that each rate is the sum of the 120 thread rows after its I row.

segments.heading: Function `hm`: time of day as text
segments.text: Turns a time stamp such as `2026-11-17T22:12:14Z` into `22:12 UTC`. With `date` true it puts the date in front: `2026-11-17 22:12 UTC`.

segments.heading: Function `n7200`: the text of n at 7200 MT/s
segments.text:
Returns the text of n in four parts, for example `6 intervals / 3 processes / 3 sessions / 1 boot`.
- Part 1: the number of records, or the number of pairs when `pairs` is given.
- Part 2: the number of processes (different values of `proc_key`).
- Part 3: `no session` when all records belong to control I or F72d12. Else it gives the sessions of the records: a count such as `3 sessions`, or the session numbers such as `sessions 1 and 3`.
- Processes without a session number are added to part 3 as extra processes, for example `3 sessions and 1 extra process`. In the rerun this is the extra part C process T72C4.
- Part 4: the fixed text `1 boot`. Line 312 asserts that all used 7200 MT/s records come from one boot.

segments.heading: Function `n8000`: the text of n at 8000 MT/s
segments.text: The same text without the session part: intervals (or pairs), processes, and the fixed text `1 boot`. Example: `11 intervals / 7 processes / 1 boot`. Line 313 asserts that all used 8000 MT/s records come from one boot.

segments.heading: Function `pairs_in_process`: pair old and load-only intervals
segments.text:
Builds the pairs for question Q1 from two record lists of a bwx runner.
- It goes through the load-only intervals `news`, sorted by launch time and round.
- For each one it takes the intervals of `olds` with the same `proc_key` and the same `round`. The script stops unless exactly one exists.
- The result is a list of pairs (old-kernel interval, load-only interval). Both intervals of a pair come from one process and one round of the kernel sequence.
- The order inside the round is not tested. In part L and in cfwd the old kernel is timed before the load-only loop of the pair. In crev it is timed after it.

segments.heading: Functions `drop` and `drops_of`: the drop in percent
segments.text: `drop` returns `(1 - new / old) x 100`: by how many percent the rate `new` lies below the rate `old`. `drops_of` returns the drop of every pair, with the old-kernel rate as `old` and the load-only rate as `new`. Both rates come from `val`. They are not rounded to 0.01 GB/s before the division.

segments.heading: Function `drop_txt`: text of a list of drops
segments.text: Rounds the lowest and the highest drop of the list to 0.1 % with `f1`. It returns `lowest % to highest %`, or a single value when both rounded values are equal. Example: `30.5 % to 31.2 %`.

segments.heading: Question Q1: the drops of the bwx12 pairs
segments.text:
`Q1` gets one entry per group of pairs.
- `C_ao`: part C, `read` directly after `oldread`, paired with `oldread`. `C_aa`: part C, `read` directly after `asmread`, paired with `oldread`.
- `L`, `I`, `F`, `L1`: `asmread` at position 1 paired with `oldread` at position 0, for part L, control I, F72d12 and the 8000 MT/s row L-1.
- The script stops unless the six groups have 4, 4, 6, 4, 2 and 2 pairs.
- Each entry gets `drops` (one drop per pair), `old` (the range of the old-kernel intervals of its pairs) and `new` (the range of its load-only intervals).
- So `old` of `C_ao` holds only the 4 `oldread` intervals of the cfwd processes, and `old` of `C_aa` only the 4 of the crev processes.
- Saved output of a build: `C_ao` 30.5 % to 31.2 %, `C_aa` 29.7 % to 31.1 %, `L` 29.2 % to 30.5 % [Ref5].

segments.heading: Function `a_pair`: one pair of part A processes
segments.text:
- In part A the two kernels run in two processes, one per binary.
- `a_pair` builds the range of the round `rnd` for the old binary (`o`) and for the new binary (`n`).
- The script stops unless each range has 3 intervals of 1 process.
- The drop is computed between the two medians. With 3 intervals the median is the middle one of the 3 rates. It is not always the second interval in time.
- Example: in session 1, round 1 the 3 rates of `bw_old` are 467.83, 467.92 and 465.38 GB/s in time order. The median is 467.83 GB/s, the first interval [Ref3].

segments.heading: Question Q1: drops of part A, test of all drops
segments.text:
- `A_PAIRS`: one pair per session (1 to 3) and round (1, 2) of part A at 7200 MT/s, so 6 pairs.
- `A8_PAIRS`: one pair per dataset (A-1, A-2) and round at 8000 MT/s, so 4 pairs.
- `Q1["A"]` and `Q1["A8"]` hold the drops of these pairs.
- `SAME_LINE_DROPS`: the 12 drops of part L, control I and F72d12. `ALL_7200_DROPS`: these plus the 8 drops of part C and the 6 drops of part A, so 26 drops.
- The script stops unless each of the 26 drops is above 0. So in every pair at 7200 MT/s the load-only value must lie below the old-kernel value.

segments.heading: Question Q2: the ranges of the groups
segments.text: One `Rg` object for each of 15 record groups. The name is `r` plus the name of the group: `rL_old` is the range of `L_OLD`, `rPL_asm` is the range of the pool `P_L_ASM`, `rPA_old` is the range of the pool `P_A_OLD`. `rL1_asm` is the range of `asmread` in row L-1 alone. Building a range calls `val` for each of its records.
The two fixed wordings of a comparison result. The script stops when they are not equal to the two texts that `facts.json` stores under `verdicts.rule_wordings`.

segments.heading: Function `width_pct`: width of a range in percent
segments.text: Returns `(hi - lo) / lo x 100`: the width of the range in percent of its lower end. The comment names the use: the size of a difference that a result `no difference seen` cannot exclude. The comment marks this as an estimate.

segments.heading: Function `wording`: the fixed text of one comparison
segments.text: Returns `no difference seen` when the 7200 MT/s range and the 8000 MT/s range overlap. Else it returns `differs between the 8000 MT/s boot and the 7200 MT/s boot`. So only the lowest and the highest rate of each group decide the wording.

segments.heading: Old read kernel: 7200 MT/s against 8000 MT/s
segments.text:
- The script stops unless four pairs of ranges overlap: part A with the pool A-1 to A-3, and part C, F72d12 and control I each with the `oldread` pool L-1 to L-4.
- It also stops unless the `oldread` range of part L lies fully below the pool L-1 to L-4.
- `L_OLD_NEAR`: the distance of the nearest ends, part L against the pool. It is below 0. `L_OLD_MED`: the median of part L minus the median of the pool.
- `L_OLD_NEAR_PCT`: the size of the first distance in percent of the lower end of the pool range. `L_OLD_MED_PCT`: the size of the second in percent of the pool median.
- Saved output of a build: part L 461.61 to 464.29 GB/s, pool 465.53 to 470.05 GB/s, nearest ends -1.24 GB/s, medians 6.27 GB/s apart [Ref5].

segments.heading: Load-only loop: 7200 MT/s against 8000 MT/s
segments.text:
Hard assertions on the `asmread` ranges. The script stops unless all hold:
- Line 494: part L lies fully above the pool L-1 to L-4.
- Lines 495 and 496: F72d12 lies inside the range of the pool.
- Line 497: control I lies fully above the pool.
- Line 498: part C, `asmread` directly after `oldread`, does not overlap the pool. This line does not test which of the two ranges is higher.
- Lines 499 and 500: the ranges of F72d12, part L and control I do not overlap each other.

- `VISIT_LO`, `VISIT_HI`: the lowest and the highest `asmread` rate over the three visits of the part L line in the 7200 MT/s boot (F72d12, part L, control I). `VISIT_OLD_LO`, `VISIT_OLD_HI`: the same for `oldread`.
- `DIST`: three kinds of distance for the `asmread` range of part L. In each pair the first value is against the pool L-1 to L-4, and the second is against F72d12.
- `nearest`: the distance of the nearest ends. `medians`: the difference of the medians. `farthest`: the distance of the farthest ends.

segments.heading: Part A, new read kernel: session 1 against A-1 and A-2
segments.text:
For each round (1 and 2), with kernel `read` of `bw_new`:
- `r7`: the range of the intervals of session 1. `r8`: the range of the intervals of A-1 and A-2 of the same round.
- Line 513: the script stops unless `r7` holds 3 intervals of 1 process and `r8` holds 6 intervals of 2 processes.
- Line 514: the script stops unless `r7` lies fully above `r8`. `near` is the distance of the nearest ends.
- `p7` and `p8`: the pass counts of the intervals (field `passes`). The script stops unless the 3 intervals of session 1 have one pass count per round.
- Sessions 2 and 3 are not compared here. The comment names the rule: V3.

`LOWEST_ASM` is the record with the lowest `asmread` rate of the pool L-1 to L-4. `rPL_asm_wo` is the range of the pool without this one interval. The script stops unless the lowest `asmread` rate of part L is above the highest rate of this smaller pool. The comment says that the section on the machine state uses the result.

`A_OLD_BELOW` and `A_OLD_ABOVE`: the part A intervals of the old read kernel with a rate below the lowest rate, or above the highest rate, of the pool A-1 to A-3. `A_OLD_W7` and `A_OLD_W8`: the width (highest minus lowest) of the 7200 MT/s range and of the pool range. The script stops unless both lists hold at least one record and the 7200 MT/s range is the wider one.

segments.heading: Function `one_process`: name the process of 3 intervals
segments.text: The script stops unless the list has exactly 3 records with one session, one round and one `proc_key`. The function then returns the text `session s, round r`. Later code calls it for `A_OLD_BELOW` and for `A_OLD_ABOVE`.

segments.heading: Part C against the rows of the older runner bwx
segments.text:
- Line 540: the script stops unless the part C intervals of `asmread` directly after `read` are all at position 2 of `cfwd.csv`.
- Lines 541 and 542 build the ranges of four groups: `C_ASM_AR`, `X_READ_AO`, `X_READ_AA`, `X_ASM_AR`.
- `X_PAIRS` puts each of three part C ranges next to the bwx range with the same kernel and the same kernel directly before.
- The script stops unless each part C range lies fully above its bwx range. `X_ABOVE` holds the three distances of the nearest ends.

- `X_MAX_READ`, `X_MAX_ASM`: the highest `read` rate and the highest `asmread` rate of all records of `X_LOADS`.
- Line 548: the script stops unless these two maxima are upper ends of the three bwx ranges of line 542. So no `asmread` interval at position 5 holds a higher rate than the highest one at position 2.
- `X_REV_MAX_READ`, `X_REV_MAX_ASM`: the highest rates of the reverse-order processes. The script stops unless each is above the maximum of `X_LOADS` for the same kernel.
- Lines 551 to 553: the script stops unless the highest reverse-order `read` rate lies inside both `read` ranges of part C, and the highest reverse-order `asmread` rate lies inside the `asmread` range of part L.

segments.heading: Function `md_sections`: split `FACTS.md` into sections
segments.text:
- It goes through the text line by line. A line that starts with `## ` or `### ` is a heading and starts a new section.
- The key of a section is the number at the start of its heading, for example `0`, `3.4` or `4.9`. A heading without a number gets the key `#` plus its text.
- The lines below a heading, up to the next heading of these two levels, are the text of the section. So the text of section `3` ends where section `3.1` starts.
- Lines before the first heading are dropped.
- It returns a dictionary from key to section text.
